cards.front: When do you use the subjunctive in Spanish?
cards.back:
Use the subjunctive after expressions of wish, desire, need, emotion, or doubt — especially when two different subjects are involved.
Key triggers: querer que, necesitar que, esperar que, pedir que
cards.grammarNote: The subjunctive is a mood, not a tense. It expresses subjectivity — things wished for, feared, doubted, or commanded — rather than objective facts.

cards.front:
Present subjunctive: yo form of -AR verbs
(e.g. atacar → ataque)
cards.back:
Start from the yo indicative → drop -o → add opposite vowel endings
ataco → atac- → ataque
tirar → tiro → tire
lanzar → lanzo → lance
cards.grammarNote: The subjunctive of -AR verbs uses -e endings (the 'opposite' of the indicative -a endings). Spelling changes that appear in the yo indicative carry into the subjunctive: atacar → ataco → ataque (c→qu).

cards.front:
Present subjunctive: yo form of -ER/-IR verbs
(e.g. correr → corra, subir → suba)
cards.back:
Start from yo indicative → drop -o → add opposite vowel endings (-a)
corro → corr- → corra
subo → sub- → suba
curo → cur- → cure
cards.grammarNote: -ER and -IR verbs use -a endings in the subjunctive (opposite of their indicative -e endings). Irregular yo forms carry through: tener → tengo → tenga; hacer → hago → haga.

cards.front:
I want the wizard to cast a spell.
(querer que + subjunctive)
cards.back: Quiero que el mago lance un hechizo.
cards.grammarNote: **querer que + subjunctive** = to want someone to do something. Two different subjects require the subjunctive: 'I' want, 'the wizard' casts. If the subject is the same, use infinitive: **Quiero lanzar un hechizo** (I want to cast a spell).

cards.front:
I need you to roll the dice.
(necesitar que + subjunctive)
cards.grammarNote: **necesitar que + subjunctive** = to need someone to do something. **tires** = tú present subjunctive of **tirar**: tire, tires, tire, tiremos, tiréis, tiren.

cards.front:
I hope the paladin survives.
(esperar que + subjunctive)
cards.grammarNote: **esperar que + subjunctive** = to hope that… **sobreviva** is the subjunctive of **sobrevivir** (to survive): sobrevivo → sobreviva.

cards.front:
Jeffrey asks his brothers to be quiet during the narration.
(pedir que + subjunctive)
cards.back: Jeffrey les pide que estén callados durante la narración.
cards.grammarNote: **pedir que + subjunctive** = to ask/request that someone do something. **estén** is the subjunctive of **estar**: esté, estés, esté, estemos, estéis, estén — irregular because **estar** has an irregular yo form (**estoy → esté**).

cards.back: haga, hagas, haga, hagamos, hagáis, hagan
cards.grammarNote: **hacer** has an irregular yo: **hago** → subjunctive stem **hag-** + subjunctive endings. Context: **Necesito que el guerrero haga algo** (I need the warrior to do something).

cards.back: tenga, tengas, tenga, tengamos, tengáis, tengan
cards.grammarNote: **tener** irregular yo: **tengo** → subjunctive stem **teng-** + endings. Context: **Quiero que el grupo tenga más puntos de vida** (I want the party to have more hit points).

cards.front: Subjunctive of PODER (to be able to)
cards.back: pueda, puedas, pueda, podamos, podáis, puedan
cards.grammarNote:
**poder** is o→ue stem-changing; this carries into the subjunctive for all forms except nosotros and vosotros: **pueda** (yo), **podamos** (nosotros).
Context: **Espero que el mago pueda curar al guerrero** (I hope the wizard can heal the warrior).

cards.back: sea, seas, sea, seamos, seáis, sean
cards.grammarNote: **ser** is fully irregular in the subjunctive — no connection to the yo indicative form (**soy**). Context: **Quiero que la campaña sea épica** (I want the campaign to be epic).

cards.back: esté, estés, esté, estemos, estéis, estén
cards.grammarNote: **estar** subjunctive adds a written accent on all forms except nosotros/vosotros. Context: **Necesito que el guerrero esté listo** (I need the warrior to be ready).

cards.front:
I hope Jeffrey rolls a twenty!
(ojalá + subjunctive)
cards.grammarNote:
**Ojalá (que) + subjunctive** = I hope / If only — from Arabic **law sha' Allah** (if God wills). No additional trigger verb is needed; **ojalá** stands alone and always takes the subjunctive.
**saque** = subjunctive of **sacar** (c→qu before e): saque, saques, saque…

cards.front:
I want the ranger to attack first.
(D&D battle scenario)
cards.back: Quiero que el explorador ataque primero.
cards.grammarNote: **ataque** = tú/él/ella present subjunctive of **atacar** (c→qu before e). Battle commands to other party members through Jeffrey as DM: **quiero que + subjunctive** tells someone what role they should play.

cards.front:
The party needs the wizard to heal everyone.
(D&D healing scenario)
cards.back: El grupo necesita que el mago cure a todos.
cards.grammarNote:
**cure** = subjunctive of **curar** (regular -ar): cure, cures, cure, curemos, curéis, curen.
**a todos** = everyone — **personal a** + **todos** (all/everyone). The personal **a** is used before human direct objects.
